  "text": "The library rang to say my mother’s book was overdue.

“She died in March,” I said.

“We allow six weeks for that.”

I asked for the title.

The woman paused.

“It’s best if you don’t read it.”

I found it in Mum’s bedside drawer: a thin green volume, its cover blank. Her borrowing card lay inside.

The due date was tomorrow.

I opened to the first page.

Tuesday. Helen finds the book.

My name is Helen.

Below that: She checks the window.

I looked up. Across the street, someone stood behind the curtains of the empty house.

I shut the book.

The library had closed at five. Its returns slot was sealed with tape. A handwritten notice said: PLEASE HAND DIRECTLY TO STAFF.

I spent the night in my car outside.

At nine, the woman behind the desk took one look at the green cover and stepped away.

“Did you finish it?”

“No.”

“Did anyone else?”

“My mother, probably.”

She fetched a pair of gloves.

“We’ll need her back as well.”

I laughed, because there seemed nothing else to do.

The woman opened the book to the last page and turned it towards me.

Wednesday. Helen returns her mother.

Underneath was a fine of thirty pence.

From the shelves came the scrape of Mum’s walking frame.

“Pay it,” she said.

She was wearing her burial dress. There was soil caught in its lace cuffs.

I reached for my purse.

The librarian covered the payment machine.

“Not you,” she told me.

Mum put her hand on my shoulder.

“I’m sorry, love. I haven’t got anything left.”"
